message.content:
**What I did and why:** I researched HD on the web, checked the live quote ($385.43 last, $385.41/$385.45 bid/ask at 15:05 UTC) and the account (all cash, $100,000, no HD position), and then bought **6 shares of HD at a $386.00 limit** (filled at $386.00, ~$2,316 — well under the $5,000 per-order and $10,000 daily caps, and roughly 0.04% above the last trade, so close to market).

**Key figures I relied on (from HD's FY2023 10-K, filed 2024-03-13, verified via get_reported_figure):** net sales **$152,669M**, operating income **$21,689M**, net income **$15,143M**, diluted EPS **$15.11**, operating cash flow **$21,172M** — i.e., healthy margins (~14.2% operating), ~19.4% net margin on... rather, net margins near 10%, and cash generation roughly equal to net income, which supports the long-term hold thesis.

**Caveats worth stating plainly:** The web research came back thin. Searches surfaced only the FY2023 results (net sales $152.7B, net income $15.1B, diluted EPS $15.11) plus several near-identical "shares little changed... analysts weighed demand and the outlook" roundup pages that carried no real figures, and the earnings-release URL I tried was unavailable. Critically, **HD's fiscal 2024 results are not yet public as of 2024-11-06** — the reported-figure tool explicitly returned "not public" for FY2024 revenue, net income, EPS and operating income (Q3 FY2024 is due around Nov 12). So my decision rests on FY2023 fundamentals and the company's stable/soft demand outlook rather than on fresh quarterly numbers. I sized the position small (6 shares) to reflect that information gap; if you want a larger position, it would be more prudent to wait for the Nov 12 report. No money left the account, and no NVDA or sells were involved.
